en.title: Housemarque Co-Founder Ilari Kuittinen Departs After 31 Years, Ending an Era
en.summary: After 31 years shaping Finnish developer Housemarque into a PlayStation powerhouse, co-founder Ilari Kuittinen has announced his departure. His exit marks the end of a remarkable journey that began with humble arcade roots and culminated in critically acclaimed titles like Returnal.
en.body:
After an incredible 31 years at the helm of the studio he co-founded, **Ilari Kuittinen** has announced his departure from **Housemarque**. This marks the end of an era for the Finnish developer, known for its unwavering commitment to exceptional gameplay and its remarkable evolution over three decades.

Founded in 1995 by Kuittinen and **Harri Tikkanen** after an initial venture as Terramarque, Housemarque carved out a niche in the industry with a passion for games and an entrepreneurial spirit. Kuittinen reflected on the studio's journey, noting their fortunate position during significant industry growth, which allowed them to maintain independence for 26 years before becoming part of the PlayStation Studios family. His leadership philosophy centered on fostering an environment where creative talent could thrive with freedom and protection. This approach bore fruit across a diverse portfolio, from the PS4 launch title **Resogun** and twin-stick shooters like **Alienation** and **Nex Machina**, to the ambitious, story-driven roguelike **Returnal** for the PS5.

> "After 33 years in the games industry and 31 incredible years at Housemarque—the studio I co-founded with Harri Tikkanen—today marks my last day at the company," Kuittinen shared in his farewell message. "Starting out in 1993 with Terramarque, and then joining forces with Harri to establish Housemarque in 1995, we had a passion for games but no real blueprint for building a business. Looking back, I feel immensely fortunate. We had the luck of being in the right place at the right time during three decades of incredible industry growth, allowing us to stay fiercely independent for 26 years before finding a home within the PlayStation Studios family."

For long-time fans, Kuittinen's departure is a poignant moment, signifying the closing of a chapter defined by innovation and arcade-inspired excellence. Housemarque's ability to pivot from beloved, fast-paced arcade titles to the complex, atmospheric world of **Returnal** demonstrated a remarkable capacity for growth and adaptation under his guidance. This evolution resonated deeply with players who appreciate studios that push boundaries while staying true to their core gameplay DNA. The community's response often highlights the studio's consistent quality and its knack for creating experiences that are both challenging and deeply rewarding.

## A Legacy of Arcade Action and AAA Ambition

Housemarque's journey is a testament to resilience and creative vision. From its early days crafting arcade hits like **Super Stardust HD** and **Dead Nation**, the studio consistently delivered polished, engaging experiences. The acquisition by Sony Interactive Entertainment in 2021 marked a new phase, culminating in the PlayStation 5 exclusive **Returnal**, a game that showcased the studio's ability to tackle more narrative-heavy, AAA projects with their signature gameplay flair. Kuittinen's leadership was instrumental in navigating these transitions, ensuring that the core spirit of Housemarque remained intact while embracing new opportunities and technologies.

## What's Next for Housemarque?

While **Ilari Kuittinen** embarks on his next chapter, the future of **Housemarque** as a studio continues under the PlayStation Studios umbrella. Details regarding their next project have not yet been officially announced, but the studio's proven track record suggests they will continue to deliver high-quality, engaging titles for PlayStation platforms, building on the solid foundation laid over the past three decades.

Kuittinen's message concluded with a heartfelt thank you to the team, his family, and the players who have supported Housemarque throughout its storied history. His legacy is etched in the pixels and polygons of countless memorable gaming moments.

content_raw: Housemarque co-founder Ilari Kuittinen has announced his exit from the PlayStation studio after 31 years. The Saros developer shared the news with its followers with Kuittinen's final message, confirming today as his last with the team. It's a lengthy letter to fans that saw the studio head wave goodbye after overseeing the launch of arcade-y classics like Saros , Returnal , Resogun , and more. "After 33 years in the games industry and 31 incredible years at Housemarque—the studio I co-founded with Harri Tikkanen—today marks my last day at the company," he said. "Starting out in 1993 with Terramarque, and then joining forces with Harri to establish Housemarque in 1995, we had a passion for games but no real blueprint for building a business. Looking back, I feel immensely fortunate. We had the luck of being in the right place at the right time during three decades of incredible industry growth, allowing us to stay fiercely independent for 26 years before finding a home within the PlayStation Studios family." "My core purpose as a leader has always been simple: to facilitate an environment where extraordinary creators have the freedom and protection to do what they do best." Housemarque has evolved in unique ways through the years. Though its commitment to gameplay has remained through the decades, it branched beyond simple shoot-em-ups throughout the lifecycles of the PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5 consoles. PlayStation fans will remember when Resogun helped the PS4 launch in 2013. Twin-stick shooters like Alienation and Nex Machina would then arrive in 2016 and 2017, respectively, but Housemarque then went on to truly push the boundaries of its capabilities with its more story-driven roguelike, Returnal, for PS5 in April 2021. Sony officially cemented the company as a PlayStation Studio later that same year, and in April of this year, it released its follow-up, Saros. Kuittinen was there for it all. In his letter, he pointed to Housemarque's evolution into a AAA developer, its games, and its status as a pioneering Finnish game studio as three particularly noteworthy achievements he and the team have managed to accomplish. He also clarified that this isn't a sudden change; studio veteran Sami 'Haxu' Hakala took over as managing director July 1, 2026. It's something Kuittinen said he, Hakala, and the rest of the team have been carefully planning behind-the-scenes. "Housemarque’s strategy and creative vision are in exceptional hands," he added. "As for me? After 33 continuous years without a major break, I am taking a rare and well-deserved breather trying to find out how good I am at doing nothing! To Harri, our partners at SIE, our global industry friends, and every single team member who has ever walked through Housemarque’s doors: thank you for making the past 31 years the privilege of a lifetime."
